correctness.rationale: For any classes C,D, the coefficient of (i,j) in the class-sum product is r_C(i)c_D(j). Summation over all second (respectively first) classes proves necessity of identical row (respectively column) profiles inside each block, and equality of profiles is sufficient. Each of the Bell(9)=21147 set partitions is visited exactly once via canonical restricted-growth strings. Both included independently implemented checkers exhaust all of them and obtain 42 qualifying partitions with class-count multiplicities 1,12,4,9,9,6,1; the direct checker enumerates all 60 subgroups of S3xS3 and proves that their distinct orbit partitions exhaust the 42. The profile checker independently verifies full stabilizer transitivity. Each yields 12 automorphism-equivalence classes with the listed orbit sizes, and the direct checker proves exactly 25 direct-product partitions. Both programs were run from actual included files and printed VERIFY_OK; outputs matched recorded files.

value.rationale: The three-by-three rectangular band is the first square nontrivial case beyond published semigroup-size-seven tables and a separate two-row family. Its complete labeled and isomorphism classification fills a concrete natural gap: 42 Schur partitions (12 automorphism types), exactly 17 not obtainable as direct product partitions, yet all 42 are automorphic. This addresses the precise distinction between automorphic and direct-product constructions highlighted in the motivating paper, with a reproducible finite certificate and explicit list of natural equivalence-class representatives. The contribution is a complete natural finite classification rather than a routine single-table recomputation.
